title: You counted 4 here and the number says 1 — what is your eye using?
question: In B you counted 4. What is telling you they are four — the separate trunks, the crown outlines, the gaps of sky, colour, something else? One sentence is enough.
context_md:
**Your counts settled it: the metric failed, and §Z is cards-only now.** You said A-2, B-4, C-3 with the founder counts withheld. Here are the two that matter, with the counts revealed:

| | founders | you counted | the metric said |
|---|---|---|---|
| **B** | 4 | **4 — all of them** | **100% fused, one mass** |
| **C** | 3 | 3 | 38% fused, separate |

**B is where it breaks.** The metric counts connected foliage and looks for columns of clear sky. In B the four crowns touch, so it finds neither — it reads the strongest possible "this is one mass" on a stand you read as four obvious trees. No amount of tuning fixes that, because the thing you are seeing is not an empty column.

So this is not a request to re-judge anything — it is the one question that would tell whoever builds the next attempt **what quantity to measure**. If it is the trunks, that is countable. If it is crown outline, that is much harder and worth knowing before someone spends a week on it.

No rush; §Z is recorded as judged by eye either way.
